findings.location: scripts/i05_gate_channel.py: Gate._drain (lines 555-564: any state other than ACTIVE or INSPECTING gets {'drain': state} back at once), Gate._settle_drain (566-571: only acts in DRAINING or HELD), Gate._urgent, and the refusal return in Gate._op_action_outcome that skips _settle_drain. README Decision 8 ('the generation becomes CLOSED once no consumed action lacks a terminal record (the A3 fence) ... the drain is then no longer pending') and the N9 disposition ('drainPending cleared after the drain'). Resolved section 2.4 WRITE_BEGIN ('replies only after the A3 drain fence (section 3.2) holds'), section 3.2 A3, counterexample 18.
findings.finding:
After an urgent close, the gate-side drain does not follow the A3 fence.
(a) A pending drain never settles. Probe PA: CREATE in flight; DRAIN_REQUEST -> {denied: [], drain: DRAINING}; CLOSE_GENERATION(REVOCATION) -> OK INVALIDATED; UPSTREAM 201 -> DELIVERED_RESULT, relayed true; ACTION_OUTCOME -> DELIVERED_RESULT, admittedBeforeInvalidation true. GENERATION_STATUS then reports state INVALIDATED with drainPending true, and stays that way. No DRAINED record is ever written, ARM is refused DRAIN_PENDING instead of NOT_ACTIVE, and the pending WRITE_BEGIN is never answered. EXPIRY and PEER_FAILURE closes behave the same way. RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED does settle, because it ends HELD.
(b) A new WRITE_BEGIN is answered without the fence. Probe PA3: CREATE in flight; CLOSE_GENERATION(REVOCATION); DRAIN_REQUEST -> {drain: INVALIDATED} at once, while action 1 is still CONSUMED with no TERMINAL record. If W02c's I07 treats that reply as the end of the drain, a policy write commits while an admitted action lacks a durable terminal classification, which section 2.4 and A3 forbid for I07 writes. The A4 qualifier is set, so no unqualified DELIVERED_RESULT becomes false.
(c) Probe Q3: DRAINING with a CREATE in flight; STORAGE_FAIL_NEXT; ACTION_OUTCOME -> REFUSED STORAGE_FAILURE. The gate is then HELD with drainPending true and nothing in flight, until the broker retries the seal (the retry records DRAINED HELD).
The depth-7 exhaustive search reached these states from every start state, for example 92 'drain reply INVALIDATED while in flight' nodes and 3,282 'drainPending in INVALIDATED with nothing in flight' nodes from start state S4.
findings.requiredChange:
Define the gate-side drain in every state.
- A pending drain settles once no consumed action lacks a terminal record: write DRAINED, clear drainPending and answer I07. This applies in INVALIDATED (and after a refused seal), not only in DRAINING or HELD.
- A WRITE_BEGIN that arrives in INVALIDATED or DRAINING either waits for the same fence or gets an answer that W02c must treat as 'no write'.
- Refuse ARM with NOT_ACTIVE outside ACTIVE once the generation has been invalidated.
- Add vectors for (a), (b) and (c).

findings.location: scripts/i05_gate_channel.py: Gate.__init__ (lines 251-253: manifest-digest uniqueness checked only within one generation's config), Gate._upstream (lines 547-549: observed_uids also taken from GET 200), Gate._op_arm_action UID_NOT_OBSERVED. README Decision 10 ('A later generation cannot re-bind the old run ... and can arm only its own run's manifests, so cleanup of an earlier run's resources is not done through I05'), the per-field table row recordedUid ('CREATE 201 or GET 200'), and the N4 disposition. I02 BROKER_HANDOFF_READINESS ('a digest belongs to one case only, so cleanup never permits name reuse'; 'Only server-recorded created names/UIDs may be cleaned'). Base section 5 (CLEANUP_PENDING until externally authorized reconciliation).
findings.finding:
A DELETE UID may come from the gate's own GET 200 of a name. The gate checks only that a manifest digest is unique within the current config. So a later run can observe and delete an earlier run's object through I05, contrary to Decision 10.
- Probe PD (one generation): run-two's Pod manifest has a different digest but the same name 'probe-pod' as run-one's M1. The config is accepted. E1/run-one CREATE M1 -> 201, UID u1, sealed. BIND E2/run-two -> OK. GET D1 -> 200, observes u1. ARM DELETE D1 with u1 -> OK. REQUEST -> FORWARD 'DELETE /api/v1/namespaces/planeon-qual/pods/probe-pod' with precondition u1.
- Probe PE (cross-generation): the generation-2 config has priorBindings {run-one, E1} and run-three, whose manifests include run-one's digest M1. The config is accepted and BIND run-three -> OK. GET M1 observes u1, then ARM DELETE M1 with u1 -> OK and FORWARD. CREATE M1 would also be armable.
All of this needs signed inputs that reuse a name or digest across runs, which I02 forbids. The effect is limited to a GET and a UID-preconditioned DELETE of a signed-name object. The gate's defensive check is still weaker than the README claims, and the GET-observed path adds no capability the design needs: a CREATE whose outcome is ambiguous already holds the generation.

findings.location: scripts/i05_gate_channel.py: Gate._storage_failure (lines 288-298: denies through _deny_armed and discards the list); the callers' second _deny_armed in Gate._urgent, Gate._op_close_generation (NORMAL_DRAIN), Gate._expire and Gate._drain. vectors.json T58: deniedActionIds changed from [1] (round 2) to []. README operation table (CLOSE_GENERATION: 'resulting state and the actions this close denied') and durable journal ('the operation then refuses or reports what it did').
findings.finding:
This regression came with the round-3 N2 fix. When a record fails during an operation, the storage-failure path denies the armed action, and the operation then reports that it denied nothing.
Probes:
- PB: ARM 1 GET; STORAGE_FAIL_NEXT; CLOSE_GENERATION(REVOCATION) -> {state: HELD, deniedActionIds: []}. The journal shows [INVALIDATED STORAGE_FAILURE HELD], [DENIED 1]. Without the failure the same close reports [1].
- PB2: the same with NORMAL_DRAIN -> [].
- PB3: EXPIRE -> {denied: []}; DRAIN_REQUEST -> {denied: [], drain: HELD}.
T58 now pins the false value. Counts: 15 occurrences in the randomized campaign and 2,085 nodes in the depth-7 search from S3. The broker still learns NOT_FORWARDED through ACTION_OUTCOME, so no classification is false. The gate's own response does contradict its journal.
findings.requiredChange: Return the storage-failure path's denied list to the caller and merge it into deniedActionIds and the EXPIRE/DRAIN outputs. Restore T58 to [1], and add EXPIRE and DRAIN vectors.

findings.location: Gate._rebuild (journal is the only input; a failed write leaves no trace) and Gate._storage_failure (the INVALIDATED record is only attempted). README durable journal, restart paragraph. Base section 5 ('partial write, readback mismatch, full disk or lost protected history starts denied and HELD').
findings.finding:
If the urgent INVALIDATED record also fails, a restart can come back CLOSED or INVALIDATED although the gate was HELD in memory.
Probes (PC):
- Clean NORMAL_DRAIN close; STORAGE_FAIL_NEXT x2; CLOSE_GENERATION(RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED) -> OK HELD, but the journal still ends [CLOSED NORMAL_DRAIN CLOSED]; GATE_RESTART -> restartState CLOSED.
- The same with CHANNEL_LOST -> ORDERLY: in memory HELD, restart CLOSED.
- After REVOCATION, a malformed frame with two failures: restart INVALIDATED.
In the depth-7 search every such divergence had at least two failures on its path (for example S3: 257 with two, 55 with three, 9 with four). The randomized campaign hit it 16 times. No ambiguous or unsealed action is ever hidden: a CONSUMED action without a TERMINAL record still rebuilds as IO_AMBIGUOUS and HELD. What is lost is the HELD caused by the storage failure itself and the broker's RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED, which the gate acknowledged although it was not durable.
findings.requiredChange: State that a restart after any write failure that could not be recorded starts HELD. For example, detect a torn or failed tail, or keep a failure marker in a separate failure domain. Otherwise, disclose the residual against base section 5, and say that the OK HELD answer to RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED is not durable in that case.

findings.location: outcome-mapping.json CREATE and DELETE DELIVERED_RESULT rows with httpStatus '4xx'; README outcome table ('4xx other than 408'); the mapping's own rule 1
findings.finding: check_agreement(CREATE or DELETE, DELIVERED_RESULT 408, DENIED) returns None (agree). The JSON rows cover 400-499, while the README and the JSON rule text say that a CREATE or DELETE 408 is never DELIVERED_RESULT. A correct gate cannot produce this (outcome_is_final(CREATE, 408) is False), so the table and the prose simply disagree. Also, the DELETE 202 row cannot be reached with the pinned DeleteOptions: the upstream delete handler returns 202 only when OrphanDependents is false (staging/.../endpoints/handlers/delete.go:188).
findings.requiredChange: Make the CREATE and DELETE class rows exclude 408, or add an explicit rule so that check_agreement refuses with M02. Optionally note that the 202 row is unreachable.

findings.location: outcome-mapping.json deleteResponseBody and deleteResponseBodySources; README 'DELETE bodies differ by kind'
findings.finding:
The cited lines check out against Kubernetes v1.37.1, both in the local tree and on raw.githubusercontent.com:
- pod/storage/storage.go:89 and service/storage/storage.go:89 set ReturnDeletedObject true;
- store.go:1458-1480 finalizeDelete returns a Status whose details carry the resource and UID.
Two gaps remain:
- The sources give file:line with no tag or commit, and the Kubernetes distribution is still unselected (W02).
- Store.Delete returns the updated object, not a Status, when deletion is not immediate (store.go:1246-1261 'return out, false, err'), for example a ConfigMap with finalizers. Probe PH: a ConfigMap DELETE 200 whose body is the object -> M05, so HELD. This fails closed and only affects liveness.
findings.requiredChange: Pin the upstream tag or commit, and require a check against the selected distribution. State the exception for deletions that are not immediate (the object body), or list it as a known HELD cause.

findings.finding: b'['*1000 + b']'*1000 (2,000 bytes) raises RecursionError, not a ValueError with an F code (depth 990 -> F00). A non-bytes input such as bytearray is reported as 'F02 frame larger than 16 KiB'. Both are still refused. N8's two named cases (B09, B10) now give F06.
findings.requiredChange: Map RecursionError to F06 (or F01), and give a distinct code to input of the wrong type.

findings.finding: T74 claims '... with an unsealed action, HELD', but only the sealed case is in the transcript. Probe Q1 confirms the behaviour: an urgent close with an unsealed delivered GET -> restart HELD. T81 claims 'an added User-Agent or Transfer-Encoding field', but only Transfer-Encoding is sent. T54 covers an extra header field in general.
findings.requiredChange: Add the missing cases or narrow the intents.

N1.evidence: outcome_is_final settles CREATE only with 201 or a 4xx other than 408, and DELETE only with 200, 202, 404 or such a 4xx. Every other status is recorded as TERMINAL IO_AMBIGUOUS with the status and digest kept as reconciliation data, the response is relayed, and the generation is HELD. T66-T69 cover CREATE 500 then drain -> HELD; a drain pending when 504 arrives -> DRAINED HELD; DELETE 503 -> HELD; CREATE 408 -> IO_AMBIGUOUS; GET 503 -> DELIVERED_RESULT. Probe Q7: DELETE 204 and 500 -> HELD. The CREATE/DELETE 5xx mapping rows are gone (A32 and A33 give M02). In the fuzz and the exhaustive search, a CREATE or DELETE with a non-final status never became DELIVERED_RESULT, and no drain or normal close settled CLOSED with an ambiguous action. The mutant with outcome_is_final always true was caught in 54 of 400 runs. Residual mapping nit: P5.

N2.evidence: Every _record failure now goes through _storage_failure: HELD, in-flight action marked, INVALIDATED attempted, armed action denied. T70 (LATE_UPSTREAM) and T71 (DRAIN_STARTED) cover the two round-2 points, and CLOSE denies an armed action in HELD. Across 3.76M fuzz events and 2.19M search nodes, an armed action never existed outside ACTIVE, the GENERATION_STATUS probe never raised, and the qualifier was never missing. The storage-failure-without-deny mutant was caught. New residual from this fix: P3 (deniedActionIds).

N3.evidence: _rebuild returns the last CLOSED, DRAINED or INVALIDATED state only when every action is sealed and terminal and none is IO_AMBIGUOUS (T72-T74, Q4), and HELD otherwise (T25, Q1, Q5). This is consistent with resolved M2. The orderly end is journalled as CHANNEL_ENDED. Every fuzzed restart (4,988) and every restart in the search kept sealed answers and classifications. Residual after two consecutive write failures: P4.

N4.evidence: Done: priorBindings refuses executionIds and run nonces bound by earlier generations (T75, both fields), the config rule refuses a digest shared by two runs (K01), the vector configs are fixed, and Decision 10 leaves cleanup of earlier runs to external reconciliation. Not enforced: name collisions between runs and digest reuse across generations still let a later run GET-observe and DELETE an earlier run's object (P2, probes PD and PE).

N5.evidence: render_request returns the exact head bytes plus the body digest. A1 compares the head and body bytes and the gate forwards its own rendering. The DeleteOptions bytes are pinned in prose, and the refusals are listed. render_request matched an independent renderer written from the Decision 4 prose for all 28 manifest, verb and UID combinations. T76-T81 each differ from the rendering only in their stated element: duplicate Host, lower-case name, HTTP/1.0, absolute-form target, %2D, Transfer-Encoding. The I04 header requirement is carried to R01 and CONF-LIVE-003. Intent nit: P8.

N6.evidence: deleteResponseBody is OBJECT for Pod and Service and STATUS for ConfigMap, and the cited upstream lines were verified (v1.37.1, local tree and raw.githubusercontent.com). The STATUS rule checks status Success, details.name, details.kind 'configmaps', details.uid, and that no resourceVersion is observed (T82, A34-A38). A Pod DELETE with a Status body -> M06. Residuals: unpinned sources and the finalizer exception (P6).

N7.evidence: RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED is in the schema enum and the model. From ACTIVE it takes the urgent path to HELD; from CLOSED or INVALIDATED it gives HELD with a record (T83, Q6: the in-flight action is qualified). Durability under two write failures: P4.

N8.evidence: A 4301-digit integer (B09) and a lone surrogate (B10) give F06. The canonical form is named and coincides with RFC 8785 for this schema: ASCII strings, integers at most 2^53-1. New residual: RecursionError for deep nesting (P7).

N9.evidence: T84 (BIND STORAGE_FAILURE) and T85 (ARM EXECUTION_NOT_BOUND) were added, and the restart qualifier rule is stated. _settle_drain clears drainPending on the normal drain path (T30, T31, T67). The status schema forbids CLOSED with an in-flight action (probe: F00). The drain left pending after an urgent close or a refused seal is the new P1.

N10.evidence: CHANNEL_LOST before the first frame closes the channel and records CHANNEL_ENDED BEFORE_FIRST_FRAME, so later frames get GENERATION_CHANNEL_USED (T86). The upstream output carries 'relayed', and the fuzz oracle confirmed relayed true only when the TERMINAL record was durable and the exchange was not lost.

questionAnswers.Q0: N1, N2, N3 and N5-N10 are CLOSED in the round-3 bytes. N4 is PARTIAL (P2). No round-1 finding reopened. P2 is next to F1 but is not a reopening: the broker still cannot supply a UID the gate did not observe; the observation itself can come from another run's object. The round-3 changes introduced or exposed P1 (drain after urgent close), P3 (deniedActionIds regression, pinned by T58) and P4 (restart after two write failures).
questionAnswers.Q3:
The table covers all six I02 outcomes and overloads none; I02 is unchanged.
- CREATE/DELETE 5xx rows are removed; unmapped statuses give M02 and a refused outcome gives M00.
- NOT_FORWARDED agrees with both DENIED and AMBIGUOUS; IO_AMBIGUOUS agrees only with AMBIGUOUS.
- Identity plus UID plus resourceVersion matching, and for a ConfigMap the Status details.name, details.kind and details.uid rule, is enough where byte equality is not required: the UID precondition, the observed resourceVersion and A2 cover the rest.
Nits: the class rows include 408 (P5); the 202 row is unreachable (P5); a ConfigMap with finalizers returns the object body and is held (P6).
questionAnswers.Q4: All ten variants are closed: additionalProperties false throughout, consts for version, direction and operation, bounded patterned strings and integers, disjoint OK and REFUSED variants, no selectors. RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED was added, and the new constraint forbids CLOSED with an in-flight action. Probes that all give F00: CLOSED with in-flight, INVALIDATED with armed, DRAINING with armed, IO_AMBIGUOUS with a status, status 99, CLOSE state ACTIVE, duplicate deniedActionIds, CLOSE refused STORAGE_FAILURE, extra fields. Combinations still allowed but unreachable: CLOSED with drainPending, DRAINING without a bound execution. INVALIDATED with drainPending is allowed and reachable (P1). decode_frame enforces canonical, duplicate-free UTF-8 of at most 16 KiB, apart from the RecursionError gap (P7).
questionAnswers.Q5:
Yes, with two intent overstatements (P8).
- Through replay(): 86/86 transcripts (outputs and final snapshots including journals), 38/38 agreement cases, 26/26 frame checks, 10/10 byte frames, and the K01 configuration refusal, all exact.
- Through my own envelope builder, which recomputed sequence and previousDigest from the gate's actual responses and re-decoded all 332 response frames with decode_frame: 86/86 exact.
- Each refused request in T05, T06, T39, T43, T48-T56 and T76-T81 differs from the armed rendering only in its stated element.
- Round-2 transcripts changed only through the round-3 rules: the relayed flag, the journal record shapes, drainPending cleared, and the run-two manifests. One of these changes is T58's deniedActionIds going from [1] to [] (P3).

Five start states: S0 bound; S1 CREATE armed with a stamped connection and a backlog entry; S2 CREATE in flight; S3 GET delivered and sealed; S4 drain pending with a CREATE in flight. Nodes: 151,842 + 434,660 + 454,297 + 881,691 + 268,057, about 2.19M, with a GENERATION_STATUS probe at every node and the same invariants as the fuzz. The only invariant breaks were in-memory HELD becoming CLOSED or INVALIDATED at restart; every one had at least two storage failures on its path (P4). Notes counted: P1 states and P3 omissions.

reviewLimit:
Read-only, source-level review by an agent separate from the author. No repository file was created or modified, and no state-changing git command, network mutation, runner, native or cloud action was taken. All scratch files are in the reviewer scratchpad.
The soundness conclusions hold only within the reference model's abstraction: REQUEST events carry pre-split head strings and body digests, journals are in-memory lists with one-shot failures (a failed write leaves no trace), the backlog is a list, and there is no real TLS, HTTP, fsync, clock, I07 handshake or broker.
The fuzzing is randomized, and the exhaustive search is bounded (depth 7, 21 events, 5 start states).
Kubernetes semantics were checked against v1.37.1 source and the public API conventions; the selected distribution is unknown.
This verdict is not an installed gate, native qualification, a C2/C3 stamping or load result, or authorization for anything installed. All E01-E12 remain OPEN_UNPROVEN. P1-P3 (MINOR) and P4-P8 (NOTE) may be carried, but they should be fixed or explicitly carried into W02c/I07 and the next revision.
